english: THE CANON OF THE MASS.
notes: Section head, set in even small capitals across the full measure above both columns.

speaker: priest
english: WE therefore, humbly pray and beseech thee most merciful Father, thro' Jesus Christ thy Son, our Lord, that thou wouldst vouchsafe to accept and bless these gifts, these presents, these holy unspotted sacrifices, which in the first place we offer thee for thy holy Catholic Church, to which vouchsafe to grant peace; as also to preserve, unite, and govern it throughout the world: together with thy servant N. our pope N. our Bishop,
notes: Two-line drop W. The book prints no cross signs anywhere in its English column; the three signs the Latin rite prescribes here are absent from both columns of this printing.

speaker: priest
english: as also all orthodox believers and professors of the catholic and apostolic Faith.
notes: The book sets this as a separate unindented block after the Bishop's N., matching the Latin column's own break at `et omnibus Orthodoxis`. Scan damage: `orthodox` prints as `ortnodox`, the h having lost its ascender; read at 1600 dpi and controlled against the facing Latin `Orthodoxis`.

english: COMMEMORATION OF THE LIVING.
notes: Set in small capitals across the full measure.

speaker: priest
english: Be mindful O Lord of thy servants, men and women, N. and N.
notes: The book prints no comma after `mindful`.

english: He prays silently for those he intends to pray for.
notes: Italic, set across the full measure.

speaker: priest
english: And of all here present, whose Faith and Devotion is known unto thee, for whom we offer. or who offer up to thee this sacrifice of praise for themselves, their families, and friends: for the redemption of their souls, for the health and salvation they hope for, and for which they now pay their vows to thee, the eternal, living, and true God.
notes: Runs over the page break at xxxiii/xxxiv. The book prints a full stop, not a comma, after `for whom we offer`, and sets a space before it; the lower-case `or` following is the book's own.

speaker: priest
english: COMMUNICATING with, and honouring in the first place, the memory of the ever glorious Virgin Mary, Mother of our Lord and God Jesus Christ: as also of the blessed Apostles and Martyrs, Peter and Paul, Andrew, James, John, Thomas, James, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Simon and Thadeus, Linus, Cletus, Clement, Xystus, Cornelius, Cyprian, Lawrence, Chrysogonus, John and Paul, Cosmas and Damian, and of all thy Saints; by whose merits and prayers grant that we may be always defended by the help of thy protection. Thro' the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
notes: `COMMUNICATING` set in small capitals. This printing has NO clause naming Saint Joseph: it passes from `Jesus Christ` to `as also of the blessed Apostles`, the name having been inserted only by the decree of 13 November 1962. `Thadeus` is the book's spelling. Right-margin ink loss on this leaf: `by the`, `protection` and `Christ` each lose their last character; all three read against the facing Latin.

english: Spreading his Hands over the Oblation he says,
notes: Italic.

speaker: priest
english: We therefore beseech thee, O Lord, graciously to accept this oblation of our servitude, as also of thy whole family; dispose our days in thy peace, preserve us from eternal damnation, and rank us in the number of thine Elect. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
notes: `We therefore` set in italic. Runs over the page break at xxxiv/xxxv. The conclusion is set out in full as `Through Christ our Lord`, not abbreviated to `Thro'` as the temporal orations of the same book usually are.

speaker: priest
english: Which oblation do thou, O God, vouchsafe in all respects, to bless, approve, ratify, and accept; that it may be made for us the body and blood of thy most beloved Son Jesus Christ our Lord.

speaker: priest
english: Who the day before he suffered, took bread into his holy and venerable hands, and with his eyes lifted up towards heaven, giving thanks to thee, Almighty God, his Father; he blessed it, brake it, and gave it to his disciples, saying: Take and eat ye all of this,
notes: Ends with a comma, the consecratory form following in the same paragraph.

speaker: priest
english: FOR THIS IS MY BODY.
notes: Set in small capitals, beginning at `FOR`. The Latin column sets `Hoc est enim Corpus meum` in the same small capitals and adds nothing after it: this printing has no counterpart to the postconciliar `quod pro vobis tradetur`.

english: After pronouncing the Words of Consecration, the Priest kneeling, adores and elevates the sacred Host.
notes: Italic, set across the full measure and turned over two lines.

speaker: priest
english: In like manner, after he had supped, taking also this excellent chalice into his holy and venerable hands, giving thee also thanks, he blessed, and gave it to his disciples, saying:
notes: Runs over the page break at xxxv/xxxvi.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Hic est enim Calix Sanguinis mei
english: TAKE AND DRINK YE ALL OF THIS FOR THIS IS THE CHALICE OF MY BLOOD OF THE NEW AND ETERNAL TESTAMENT: THE MYSTERY OF FAITH: WHICH SHALL BE SHED FOR YOU, AND FOR MANY, TO THE REMISSION OF SINS.
notes: Set in small capitals beginning at `TAKE`, so the caps extent differs from the form over the bread, which begins at `FOR`. `THE MYSTERY OF FAITH` stands INSIDE the form, as it does in the 1962 typical edition and as it does not in the 2002 Prex eucharistica I. Right-margin ink loss on this leaf: the hyphens of `CHA-LICE` and `MYS-TERY` are lost, `OF` after `MY BLOOD` loses its F, and `ETERNAL` loses its L; all read against the facing Latin.

speaker: priest
english: As often as you do these things, ye shall do them in remembrance of me.
notes: Printed as a separate paragraph after the form, not within it. Not in small capitals.

english: Here also kneeling, he adores and elevates the Chalice.
notes: Italic, set across the full measure.

speaker: priest
english: Wherefore, O Lord, we thy servants, as also thy holy people, calling to mind the blessed passion of the same Christ thy Son our Lord, his resurrection from the dead, and admirable ascension into heaven, offer unto thy most excellent Majesty of thy gifts bestowed upon us, a pure Host, a holy Host, an unspotted Host, the holy bread of eternal life, and chalice of everlasting salvation.
notes: Right-margin dropout in `salvation`, which prints `salva.ion`; read against the facing Latin `Calicem salutis perpetuae`.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Supra quae propitio ac sereno vultu
english: Upon which vouchsafe to look, with a propitious and serene countenance, and to accept them, as thou wert graciously pleased to accept the gifts of thy just servant Abel, and the sacrifice of our Patriarch Abraham, and that which thy High Priest Melchisedech offered to thee, a holy sacrifice and unspotted victim.
notes: Runs over the page break at xxxvi/xxxvii.

speaker: priest
english: We most humbly beseech thee, Almighty God, command these things to be carried by the hands of thy holy angels to thy altar on high, in the sight of thy divine Majesty, that as many as shall partake of the most sacred body and blood of thy Son at this altar, may be filled with every heavenly grace and blessing. Thro' the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
notes: Runs over the page break at xxxvii/xxxviii. The conclusion renders `Per eumdem Christum` as `Thro' the same Christ`; the 2002 Prex eucharistica I drops `eundem` and parenthesises the whole conclusion.

english: COMMEMORATION OF THE DEAD.
notes: Set in small capitals across the full measure.

speaker: priest
english: Be mindful, O Lord, of thy servants N. and N. who are gone before us with the sign of Faith, and rest in the sleep of peace.
Here particular mention is silently made of such of the Dead as are to be prayed for.
notes: Italic, set across the full measure and turned over two lines.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Ipsis, Domine, et omnibus in Christo
english: To these, O Lord, and to all that sleep in Christ grant, we beseech thee, a place of refreshment, light, and peace: through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.
notes: Runs over the page break at xxxviii; the catchword `D` stands at the foot of xxxvii and the signature `D 2` at the foot of xxxix. The conclusion is set out in full and in lower case, `through`, where the same book abbreviates elsewhere.

english: Here striking his Breast, the Priest says,
notes: Italic, set across the full measure.

speaker: priest
english: Also to us sinners, thy servants, confiding in the multitude of thy mercies, vouchsafe to grant some part and fellowship with thy holy apostles and martyrs; with John, Stephen, Matthias, Barnabas, Ignatius, Alexander, Marcelline, Peter, Felicitas, Perpetua, Agatha, Lucy, Agnes, Cecily, Anastasia, and with all thy saints: into whose company we beseech thee to admit us, not in consideration of our merit, but of thy own gratuitous pardon. Through Christ our Lord.
notes: `Marcelline` and `Cecily` are the book's forms. The book prints NO Amen after this conclusion, as the 1962 typical edition also does not.

speaker: priest
english: By whom, O Lord, thou dost always create, sanctify, quicken, bless, and give us all these good things.
notes: The facing Latin prints `semper bona ereas` for `creas`, the c having failed; the English `create` is undamaged and controls the reading.

speaker: priest
latin_incipit: Per ipsum, et cum ipso, et in ipso
english: By him and with him, and in him, is to thee, God the Father Almighty, in the unity of the Holy Ghost all honour and glory
notes: The book prints no full stop after `glory`; the sentence is completed by the following versicle at the head of xxxix. The five cross signs the Latin rite prescribes here are absent from both columns.

speaker: priest
english: P. For ever and ever. R. Amen.
notes: The first two lines of xxxix, closing the Canon. The book's running head `THE CANON OF THE MASS` continues to xlii, over the Pater noster and the whole Communion rite, so the running head is not the boundary of the Canon.
